messages:
rachel: Hey team — lost my physical insurance card while in Lisbon. I have a dentist appt tomorrow and need a refill of a maintenance med (not controlled, but needs prior auth sometimes). Can I use the digital card? How fast can we get a replacement mailed to a US friend? Also worried about refill logistics abroad.
Benefits Bot: You can access your digital ID from the portal immediately: https://benefits.redwoodinc/id-card. For replacement physical cards we can request a reissue. Typical domestic mail 7-14 business days; expedited on request but depends on carrier. For urgent care, download and screenshot the digital card.
Tim (People Ops): Hi @rachel — short answers: yes, digital card is generally accepted for verification (dentists and pharmacies accept screenshots or the PDF). Steps: 1) Log into Benefits Portal > ID Cards > Download PDF; 2) If you want a new physical card mailed to a US address, reply with the mailing address and we'll submit the request.
Tim (People Ops): For the prescription refill: if the drug requires prior authorization, we can start the PA immediately, but carrier and PBM timelines vary. If you're abroad and the pharmacy needs ID, show the digital card + passport. If the med needs a new Rx from a local doc, ask the clinic for an itemized receipt and prescription; save everything for claim/PA.
rachel: Pharmacy in Lisbon asked for a physical ID and the Rx. They said foreign prescriptions are sometimes honored but they need the patient's insurance number (I gave them member ID from the portal) and a local prescriber. Is it worth trying to fill here or should I request an emergency supply from my stateside pharmacy?
Leah: I did an emergency refill in Mexico once. Carrier international assistance connected me to a local clinic that wrote a temporary prescription; the PBM paid part of it. Took a bit of emailing but worked. Always get an itemized receipt and a copy of the local prescription.
Tim (People Ops): Options: A) Try local fill — risk is OON pricing and PBM rejection; keep receipts and we'll file claims/appeal. B) Contact carrier's International Assistance (they can help with local providers and pre-cert) — number is on the digital ID PDF. C) If you can wait, ask your US pharmacy for a short-term emergency supply and have a friend overnight it or use a mail-forwarding service (note customs). D) We can submit an expedited PA to the carrier/PBM if you provide pharmacy name, Rx name and NDC if known, and prescriber info.
Pharmacy Team: Quick note from pharmacy ops: many EU pharmacies will accept the member ID + passport and the prescriber's details. If the med is brand-only, they may substitute, so ask about generics. We recommend taking a photo of the prescription and the itemized price.
rachel: Tim — please submit the replacement card to be mailed to my sister in CA: 123 Olive St, Apt 4, San Mateo, CA 94401. Also attaching the prescription photo. The med is "levothyroxine 50mcg" (not controlled).
Tim (People Ops): Got it — submitting reissue request and starting an expedited PA with PBM. If carrier allows, we ask them to email a carrier confirmation PDF you can use at the pharmacy. Expect digital confirmation within 24-72 hours for the PA; physical card request submitted (we'll request expedited mail) — usually 3-7 business days if carrier allows alternate mailing.
Benefits Bot: Replacement card request submitted. Ref: R-2026-5592. Expedited PA submitted to PBM. PA Ref: PA-2026-7714. You will receive email confirmations from the carrier/PBM.
Leah: FYI — when my PA went through for a thyroid med, the carrier sent a PDF authorization that the local pharmacy accepted as proof. If they push back, ask the pharmacist to call PBM directly with the PA ref.
rachel: Thanks all. One practical Q: should I fax anything to the carrier or just upload to the claims/PA portal? Fax is slow from here.
Tim (People Ops): Upload is best (portal handles PDFs and photos). If a carrier/PBM asks for fax, we can route it from our office. In your upload, include: member name, DOB, member ID, Rx name/dose, prescribing clinic name, and travel dates. Example upload note: 
```
Member: Rachel Torres
DOB: 1990-05-08
Member ID: XXXXX1234
Rx: Levothyroxine 50 mcg
Prescriber: Clinica Porto Saude, Dr. Silva
Travel dates: 2026-03-18 to 2026-03-30
Request: emergency refill / expedited PA
```
Pharmacy Team: If PBM denies an out-of-country claim, save the receipt and we'll help file an appeal after you return.
rachel: Uploading docs now. One last thing: will this trigger any payroll/tax adjustments? I added dependents recently and worried about imputed income showing up.
Tim (People Ops): No — a lost card/replacement or a claim won't change payroll or imputed income. Imputed income only applies when you add dependents that are tax-imputable. Good question though.
Benefits Bot: Case updates will be posted here and emailed. If you need immediate help, call International Assistance on the digital card. Reference R-2026-5592 / PA-2026-7714.
rachel: Great, thanks everyone. Will update here when pharmacy responds. :thumbsup:"
